question:
(a) Explain how the depletion region changes during forward and reverse bias of a junction diode.
(b) Use this explanation to describe how a junction diode produces rectified output in a half-wave rectifier.

options.A:
(a) Forward bias widens the depletion region and reverse bias narrows it.
(b) In a half-wave rectifier, current flows only during reverse bias.
options.B:
(a) Forward bias opposes the barrier potential, thins the depletion layer and allows majority-carrier current; reverse bias supports the barrier, widens the layer and permits only a tiny minority-carrier current.
(b) In a half-wave rectifier the diode conducts through the load during the forward-biased half-cycle and blocks during the reverse-biased half-cycle. Thus only one half of each AC cycle appears across the load as unidirectional pulsating output.
options.C:
(a) The depletion layer remains unchanged in both bias conditions.
(b) A half-wave rectifier produces an identical sinusoidal AC output.
options.D:
(a) Reverse bias makes the depletion layer disappear and produces large majority current.
(b) Both half-cycles pass through the load in opposite directions.
